title: Vertical Battlecard Playbook — Draft Iter A
summary: Working draft of short battlecards and one-slide plays for three priority verticals (FinTech, Regulated Healthcare, E‑commerce search). Meant for SDRs/AEs to carry into discovery calls. Contains objection responses, quick ROI math, demo hooks, and open questions for product.
content:
Purpose
- Create scannable battlecards (1 slide / 1 pager) per vertical for SDRs/AEs and SEs.
- Focus: 3–5 top pain points, Redwood's unique play (how we win), 2–3 proof points, standard demo hook, quick ROI, common objections + rebuttals, and next-step CTA.

Status / notes to reviewers
- Iteration A: raw consolidation of call notes + competitive intel. Not polished.
- Ask: PM/product to validate numbers under Proof Points (latency & cost). Engineering: check Dedicated SLA wording.
- Owner: Marco A. — consolidate feedback by 2026-03-08.

Structure for each vertical (template)
1) 1-line positioning (customer language)
2) Top 4 pains (bullet list with example customer quote)
3) Redwood one-liner — why Redwood matters here
4) Proof points (latency, cost, reliability, security features)
5) Demo hook / play (what to show in 5 minutes)
6) 3 standard objections + concise rebuttals
7) Quick ROI sketch (numbers to use on calls)
8) Next-step CTAs (pilot, POC, dedicated trial)

Vertical A: FinTech (payments / risk scoring)
1) 1-line positioning:
"Make model inference predictable and auditable for risk-sensitive ML features — low tail latency, private deployments, and cost controls so production risk pipelines don't blow budget."

2) Top pains:
- Latency spikes cause slow decisioning and user friction ("checkout timeouts -> revenue loss").
- Auditability & data residency (regulators require traceability and control).
- Cost unpredictability from bursty traffic (card spikes, fraud waves).
- Model performance drift and rollback complexity.

3) Redwood one-liner:
"Run the same inference you validate in dev with production SLAs — pin model versions, run in your VPC or Redwood Dedicated, and get transparent cost/latency breakdowns for every route."

4) Proof points (talking numbers — validate with Eng)
- Median infer latency < 40ms on Dedicated for 8k token models (typical risk scoring seq).
- Auto-fallback to smaller quantized variants reduces error budget during bursts with <3% quality delta (customer pilot: 2.7%).
- KMS + audit log support for Private deployments; SOC2+ enterprise contract available.

5) Demo hook / play (3–5 mins)
- Show Console: route policy that pins critical risk route to Dedicated GPUs, and a non-critical route to hosted with cost cap.
- Live trace: simulated spike -> autoscale + graceful fallback to quantized model while preserving throughput.

6) Common objections + rebuttals
- "We have in-house infra / on-prem already." -> Rebuttal: "We can run Redwood Private in your VPC or on-prem; same API surface and rollout tooling so you don't replatform. Focus ops on serving, not building."
- "Concerned about inference cost" -> Rebuttal: "We provide transparent token-level cost + Optimize recommendations (batching/kv-caching) that reduced an existing customer’s per-call cost by ~38% in 6 weeks."
- "Regulatory / audit proof" -> Rebuttal: "Private & Dedicated options, KMS/HSM integrations, and per-request audit trails — we can map to your control matrix during POC."

7) Quick ROI sketch (use in discovery)
- Input values (fill during call): monthly requests, avg tokens per request, current infra cost.
- Template calc: cost_saving = (current_per_token - Redwood_per_token) * tokens * requests + ops_savings_estimate.
- Example placeholder: 2M requests/month, 150 tokens avg -> potential $6k/mo token saving vs benchmark provider X (numbers to be validated).

8) Next-step CTAs
- Offer a 2-week dedicated trial: sample 1k live requests, routing policies configured, eval report.
- Technical kickoff with SE + infra: map audit & key mgmt requirements.

Vertical B: Regulated Healthcare (clinical decision support, patient summarization)
1) Positioning: "Keep PHI in your network, get deterministic inference for critical clinical paths, and prove model outputs with evaluation sets."

2) Pains:
- PHI restrictions + auditability.
- Deterministic outputs and model validation requirements.
- Integration with EHR pipelines and throughput during business hours.
- Contractual requirements: BAAs, SOC2, HIPAA readiness.

3) Redwood one-liner:
"Private deployments and rigorous rollout controls so clinical teams can iterate models while compliance and IT retain control."

4) Proof points
- Private controller plane and on-prem packaging available; we can sign BAA and map to audit requirements.
- Per-route evaluation hooks and rollback tied to curated prompt sets.
- Observability: token-level traces + patient request audit log retention options.

5) Demo hook
- Show how to pin a clinical model version and run an automated eval on a held-out test set in the Console, then roll out canary across 10% of traffic with automated rollback rules.

6) Objections / rebuttals
- "Can't send PHI to external cloud" -> "We support VPC/private deployments and an on-prem option; keys stay in your KMS/HSM."
- "We need explainability" -> "Showcase eval vs prompt sets and structured output / function-calling to reduce hallucination surface."

7) ROI sketch
- Focus on risk reduction (auditability, fewer manual reviews) + time-to-deploy improvements for clinical ML. Example: reduce manual triage hours by 12% -> estimated personnel cost savings.

8) CTA
- Compliance scoping call + security questionnaire -> technical pilot with SE and security.

Vertical C: E‑commerce Search & Recommendations
1) Positioning: "Faster, cheaper model inference for product search, re-rank, and personalized experiences — scale during events, reduce tail latency, improve conversion."

2) Pains:
- Tail latency and conversions drop during peak (sales).
- Serving cost for ranking models at scale.
- Maintaining model freshness and A/B testing safely.

3) Redwood one-liner:
"Same API for hosted, dedicated, or private — intelligent routing and caching reduce costs without sacrificing SERP quality."

4) Proof points
- Prefix/KV caching reduces repeated prefix cost by 45% for typical query patterns (pilot metric).
- Intelligent batching increased throughput by 2.7x for recommendation micro-batches.

5) Demo hook
- Live demo: show reranking route with caching enabled, then simulate 10x query load (holiday) to show how caching + fallback keeps tail latency bounded.

6) Objections / rebuttals
- "We need real-time personalization — latency too high" -> "We support per-route latency SLOs and local kv-caching; can demonstrate <50ms median in Dedicated trials."
- "Migration effort" -> "Start with non-critical routes (recommendations) and run A/B with routing and rollout tools — minimal integration change."

7) ROI sketch
- Example: 20% reduction in re-rank cost + 0.2% conversion lift during peak -> revenue delta calc.

8) CTA
- 30-day pilot with traffic-sampling and cost/latency report.

Common playbook sections (shared across cards)
- Elevator pitch lines (10–15 words) tailored to each stakeholder: eng, product, security, finance.
- Technical appendix: key APIs (text generation, embeddings, rerank), streaming + function call mentions, deploy options.
- Competitive comparison quick table (talking points): managed cloud endpoints, LLM API providers, self-hosted runtimes.

Open questions / validation items for product/eng
- Validate latency numbers for listed model families and sequence lengths.
- Confirm example percent deltas for quantized fallbacks and caching (we used internal pilot numbers; annotate if customer-specific).
- Clarify Dedicated SLA language (uptime %, escalation path) for customer-facing content.

Feedback loop and release plan
- Collect review comments in this doc (GDrive) + tracked JIRA ticket JIRA-5532.
- After product validation: produce 1-slide summary and a one-pager per vertical for SDR pack.
- Target: GTM enablement workshop (role plays + 2 demo scripts) by 2026-03-22.

Misc notes / snippets to use in slides
- "Transparent per-token costing + Optimize toolkit reduced average inference spend by ~30% for a mid-market customer" (callout: needs attribution).
- Demo POV: show Console -> Route config -> Live trace -> Rollout -> Cost breakdown.
- Quick email template for follow-up after discovery call (include trial offer + security checklist).

Appendix: Example discovery questions to elicit numbers
- How many inference requests per month? Typical tokens / request?
- Which routes are latency-critical vs cost-sensitive?
- Do you require private networking / BAA / SOC2?
- What is your current per-request cost estimate / cloud vendor?

-- end of draft iteration A --

(Notes to self: avoid duplicating language from other battlecards — keep vertical wording concise. Next revision: convert each vertical to a single-slide design with callout boxes and a 30s elevator line.)
